title: Crofton Measures in Hilbert Geometry
statement: Prove or disprove: in the Hilbert geometry of a convex body $C\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, a positive Crofton measure for Holmes–Thompson curve length $\operatorname{vol}_1$ exists only when the geometry is hyperbolic, equivalently when $C$ is an ellipsoid.
background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Mini-Workshop: Valuations and Integral Geometry (2010), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2010/04, pp. 141--178](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2010/04)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** The report presents the ellipsoid-only Crofton assertion as a conjecture; later work located here gives existence results in special settings but no proof or counterexample in the stated generality.
